useful_delta: Recovered the product-host boundary that the current Chat Object/worker architecture must preserve: workers and Chat Objects may compile missions, prompts, candidates and evidence, but they must not become product apply/update/rollback authority. FABRIC/Airlock should be treated as the typed admission boundary between candidate-producing cognition and the scoped host/owner that can mutate Current/Served product state. Existing durable Prometeo already supplies strong later evidence for the intended semantics: exact artifact identity by lineage+bytes/SHA, Candidate/Human Accepted/Current/Served separation, receipt-backed pointer promotion, verified served state, rollback donors/proof, scoped owners, staged CAS/idempotent migration patterns, and host-routed promotion workflows. The literal historical FABRIC/Mission Fabric/Prompt Fabric/Airlock source contract was not recovered from the current durable tree/search, so this return preserves only evidence-backed invariants and labels the exact historical contract unresolved rather than reconstructing it as canonical.

facts.claim: The current Big Picture explicitly requires recovery/interface with FABRIC identity/bytes/containment, Mission Fabric, Prompt Fabric, Airlock, host-owned apply/update authority, update/rollback, safe admission and deterministic/idempotent execution where needed; Chat Objects must extend rather than bypass these layers.

Current authority policy binds identity to lineage plus exact bytes/SHA/checkpoint, forbids authority inference from version numbers, and requires exact acceptance for Human Accepted/Current/Served pointer movement.

Cross-system invariants require Candidate, Human Accepted, Served and Archived to remain distinct; promotion is pointer movement after acceptance rather than file overwrite; rollback must be tested A-to-B-to-A with identity/state/cache-pointer restoration.

The operator contract defines product change as target resolution -> seed -> work item -> context pack -> execution -> artifact return -> verification -> candidate, followed by a separate release path Candidate -> exact verification -> Human Acceptance -> receipt-backed Current transition -> Served verification.
The current Chat Object authority law says it orchestrates and remembers while Current/Catalog/Lineage/Human Accepted/Served remain distinct authorities.

R1-B architecture recovery established that artifact returns cannot mutate Current, automatic modification must resolve a registered writable target, and release/canary/acceptance/serving/rollback/export are distinct evidence gates.

Current Graph materializes separate pointers for candidate current, human accepted candidate, served current, canary, rollback proof and export, demonstrating that apply/promotion and served verification are not one state transition.

A current host-routed promotion workflow verifies candidate bytes first, copies verified bytes into the source-of-served runtime, validates the served manifest, then commits without overwriting parallel main work.

Universal Control migration work preserves a canonical owner until shadow parity, requires additive/idempotent shadow operations, and forbids ownership cutover or Served publication until explicit parity/rollback gates pass.
The prior recovery sweep declares historical-chat replay unnecessary for recovered architecture and preserves the rule that product promotion remains a separate explicit authority process.

candidates.name: Fabric Envelope as candidate transport contract
candidates.proposal: Define FABRIC as a typed envelope for a candidate transition, not as a new global authority. Minimum fields: fabric_id/schema_version, target identity/owner, mission_ref, prompt_program_ref where relevant, artifact byte digests/provenance, requested effects/write scope, capability/privacy scope, freshness preconditions, verification requirements, idempotency/replay key, rollback anchor, and eventual admission/apply/served receipts. The envelope remains CANDIDATE until the scoped owner admits/applies it.

candidates.name: Mission Fabric vs Prompt Fabric
candidates.proposal: Mission Fabric is the model/provider-independent semantic execution contract: goal, success conditions, constraints, authority ceiling, invariants, allowed effects, expected evidence and return. Prompt Fabric is a replaceable compiled execution representation produced from Mission Fabric + Constitution/Active Method + role/job + Working Set. Prompt bytes never grant authority and may change without changing mission identity.

candidates.name: Airlock as admission boundary
candidates.proposal: Airlock validates target ownership, artifact identity/provenance, privacy/capabilities, allowed effects, freshness/preconditions, verification evidence, replay/idempotency and rollback readiness before product-host apply. Outcomes should be ADMIT, HOLD/NEEDS_EVIDENCE or REJECT with durable reason/evidence. Admission is not Human Acceptance, Current transition or Served proof.

candidates.name: Host-owned apply/update/rollback
candidates.proposal: Only the resolved product/host owner executes the authoritative mutation path. The owner applies admitted exact bytes/pointers atomically where possible, emits an apply receipt, verifies Current and independently verifies Served when applicable. Rollback uses an explicit donor/previous identity and emits its own proof; worker DONE or parent integration decision cannot substitute for these receipts.

candidates.name: Identity / bytes / containment semantics
candidates.proposal: Keep logical identity, byte identity and containment separate: logical identity says what product/capability/slot this is; byte identity says exactly which immutable payload/version is proposed; containment says which host/owner/scope may admit and activate those bytes. Replacing bytes never silently replaces logical authority, and identical labels across lineages are not equivalent.

candidates.name: Composition with current Chat Object workers
candidates.proposal: Recommended flow: Chat Object/Campaign -> Planner/Compiler -> Mission Fabric -> Prompt Fabric/Working Set -> scoped Worker -> Artifact RETURN/evidence -> Steward integration decision -> Fabric Envelope -> Airlock -> resolved Host/Owner apply -> Current receipt -> Served verification/rollback proof. Agent Network coordinates lifecycle/collisions/freshness around this flow but is not admission or product authority.

candidates.name: Do not duplicate existing packet layers
candidates.proposal: Treat JOB/Execution Packet as an existing delegated Mission-Fabric slice and Context Foundry/Working Set as Prompt-Fabric inputs. Before creating new schemas, map existing fields and add only missing cross-host admission fields. Preserve Current/Catalog/Lineage/receipts as canonical owners rather than creating FABRIC-owned duplicates.

candidates.name: Authority roles in Shared Graph
candidates.proposal: Extend shared-owner metadata to distinguish candidate_producer, integration_authority, admission_authority, apply_authority, current_pointer_owner, served_verifier and rollback_owner. One entity may hold several roles, but they must not be implicitly collapsed because the parent Chat Object coordinates the campaign.

conflicts.issue: The phrase 'parent integrates artifacts' can be misread as direct product mutation authority.
conflicts.resolution: Keep cognitive/integration acceptance separate from host apply authority: the parent/steward may accept a candidate for promotion, but the resolved product owner/Airlock executes the authoritative transition and receipts.

conflicts.issue: Workstream-level write scopes or Git permissions can be broader than a worker JOB's authority.
conflicts.resolution: The narrower durable JOB/capability grant remains authoritative for the worker; transport capability must not be interpreted as product ownership.

conflicts.issue: Current host-routed workflows can copy/promote verified bytes, while global authority policy still requires acceptance appropriate to the affected scope.
conflicts.resolution: Model technical admission/apply and Human Acceptance as separate gates. A workflow may perform a technical transition only when its scope-specific authority preconditions are satisfied.

tests_for_future_implementation: Reject scope/owner/capability mismatch even if worker transport can technically write.
Replay same admitted operation idempotently without duplicate promotion.
Bind verification to exact final bytes/digest.
Prove apply receipt is distinct from Served observation.
Exercise rollback A-to-B-to-A and verify identity/state/cache-pointer restoration.
Prove worker RETURN/DONE cannot directly move Human Accepted/Current/Served pointers.
Prove privacy classification cannot be weakened by Prompt Fabric compilation or derived context.

suggested_parent_action: During batch reconciliation, preserve a dedicated Product Host Integration layer rather than folding it into Chat Object or Agent Network. Build a mapping table from existing JOB/Execution Packet, Context Foundry, Current/Catalog/Lineage, receipts and host-routed workflows onto Mission Fabric / Prompt Fabric / FABRIC / Airlock roles. Only if gaps remain should the parent commission a shared Fabric Envelope + Airlock contract. Any implementation batch must resolve the concrete host owner first and include stale-precondition, exact-byte, idempotency, served-proof and rollback tests. Keep U15-01/U15-02 explicitly unresolved until exact historical source appears or the parent deliberately supersedes the historical naming with a new contract.
